R3-01.why: The broadest set of high-visibility, no-power sinks in the slate. Report Card poses, caught/escape emotes and Chaos finishers are shown to the whole lobby every round, which is the strongest kind of cosmetic visibility. The Parent car skin plays in a cutscene everyone watches. Host House rule is a social purchase that friends see. The Bedroom adds housing and decor, a proven Roblox sink (Bloxburg, Adopt Me), and it is giftable. Monthly houses sold as cosmetic bundles give recurring drops, and a rewarded-video Fun multiplier is low-friction. Three weaknesses: (1) In 5–7-player servers you are the Parent only about 1 round in 6, so Parent costumes, the headline item, are worn rarely and are hard to justify buying. (2) The theme of kids hiding a mess from Mom skews young, so little spend will come from age-verified US 18+ players and the +42% DevEx boost adds little. Young players are also the audience most exposed to the FTC complaint. (3) Bedroom furniture is only seen when a friend walks in, so it is a weak earner beyond gifting.
R3-01.fix: Make Parent costumes worth buying with a fair, capped Parent-queue option. For example, a 'Parent Pass' that lets you volunteer first once every few rounds, never a guarantee and with no gameplay effect, or a free rotating queue with an owned-costume preview in the lobby. Add paid private servers (party friend groups are the natural buyers), knowing Plus subscribers get them free. Let Bedroom trophies show on the lobby street (window displays) so decor is seen without a visit. Keep season-pass and house bundles free of countdown timers, with past items buyable later.

R3-02.why: Ink trails are a genuinely good cosmetic: seen on every cast and blended into fusions, so a purchase also shows up on friends' spells. Fusion and boss finishers fire at peak moments. Premium familiars sold directly are a pet-adjacent sink with good appeal, and the fixed familiar collection is earnable with no gacha. The 'second wind' revive costs a rewarded video, not Robux, so it avoids pay-to-progress. Limits: players sit on fixed balconies with an auto camera and attention on the drawing pad, so avatar outfits and familiars are on screen far less than in a free-roam game. There is no lobby social space or gifting, and Rune Book covers and tower themes are low-visibility. Gesture-input co-op roguelites are a narrower audience, which caps total revenue even if conversion is good. There is no convenience lever that doesn't touch the roguelite balance.
R3-02.fix: Add a shared hub (wizard school courtyard) where familiars, ink signatures and school robes are displayed and can be gifted. Sell 'fusion colour pairs' that only appear when two owners fuse, a social item that rewards friends who buy together. Put the revive behind a once-per-run ad only, never Robux, to stay clear of FTC pay-to-continue criticism. Offer private servers for 4-person friend groups.

R3-03.why: The cosmetic design is clever: equipping a statue skin spawns matching NPC statues, and the Unmasking credits the owner with name and signature pose, which partly fixes the core problem that in hide-in-plain-sight games your cosmetic is meant to go unnoticed. But for most of the round paid skins are camouflage nobody admires. Guard beam colours and tag effects are very visible, yet only wearable in the 1 round in 5–8 when you are the Guard. Prank-effect cosmetics are seen briefly, and the Prank Gallery frames are low-visibility. There is no gifting, no social space beyond a plaque wall, no rewarded video and no convenience lever. Disguise packs also carry a perception risk: if a paid skin blends better (more matching NPCs, better poses), players will call it pay-to-win. Expect a typical, modest cosmetic income with a single-digit-percent spender rate and low ARPPU.
R3-03.fix: Make the Unmasking and the post-round 'Caught on Camera' reel the showcase: owned reveal stingers, a slow-motion pose, a crowd reaction. Make every skin, free or paid, spawn the same number of matching NPCs, and say so in the store. Add a lobby 'museum gallery' where players' statue skins stand on display and can be gifted. Add a rewarded video (for example, extra prank reveals in the next round) and private servers.

R3-04.why: Vehicles are the game's identity and are sold directly. That gives high-perceived-value, bigger-ticket items (car and boat games show vehicles sell), with a new one every 2–3 weeks as a recurring drop. The Captain rule plus crew 'chip in' gifting is the best social-purchase mechanic in the slate: friends literally buy for the host and the whole crew rides it. Per-seat paddle skins, splash/bonk effects and blame-card emotes are on screen for the whole run. Boathouse lets friends hop into your collection. Weaknesses: under the Captain rule only one player's vehicle, skin and trail show per run, which lowers the value of buying for non-hosts. Premium vehicles have distinct handling (the balloon uses altitude), so in Versus and ranked a bought vehicle could be, or look like, an advantage. Boathouse decor is low-visibility. There is no rewarded video, and private servers are not mentioned even though a friend-crew game suits them well.
R3-04.fix: In Versus and ranked, group vehicles into handling classes that are balanced across free and paid, so premium buys a look and a seat layout, never speed. Let non-host crew show their own owned vehicle as a trailing 'escort' ghost or Boathouse banner in the lobby, so personal ownership still shows. Add private servers (crews are pre-formed friend groups) and a rewarded video for a bonus medal reroll or coin doubler. Keep vehicle launches free of countdown pressure, so each stays buyable afterwards.

R3-05.why: This is the strongest Roblox-native shape: a pet companion that follows you everywhere and rides your truck in runs, so accessories on it are high-visibility and proven (Adopt Me-style pet cosmetics). Extra companion slots are a classic, well-converting convenience item that is also earnable, and they don't frustrate play. Hose water effects are on screen constantly. Giftable accessories, truck liveries under the Captain rule, a season pass and rewarded video round it out. Animals plus firefighters has the widest appeal in the slate. Limits: ruling out paid critters gives up the biggest pet-game lever, which is ethically right but caps the top end. The audience will skew young, with low ARPPU, little qualifying adult DevEx, and the most FTC scrutiny over timers and pressure. Locker decor is low-visibility. With a fixed elevated camera, uniforms read less than companions do.
R3-05.fix: Lean into the companions: cosmetic 'variants' (colours and patterns) of critters you have already rescued, sold directly and giftable. Make rescued critters wander the shared Fire Station lobby so friends see each other's collections and accessories. Keep slots priced as a one-time pass, not a consumable. Add private servers for squads. Make seasonal critter drops earnable for the whole season with no countdown timers, and make past season items buyable later.

overall_notes: No concept here is a top-quartile Roblox earner (8+). All five are cosmetic-only by design. That is right for the 28-day-retention algorithm and the FTC climate, but with about 3.8% of players spending and a median ARPPU near $0.70, revenue depends on player volume and on how visible items are. Highly visible, social items earn: per-round lobby showcases (R3-01), gifting a captain's vehicle (R3-04), a pet companion that follows you (R3-05), and ink trails that blend in fusions (R3-02). Low-visibility items (decor rooms, plaque frames, book covers, lockers) will earn little and should not be counted on. Gaps common to all five: (1) Private servers are not listed, though every concept is a friend-group game. Plus subscribers get them free, but they still drive co-play and retention and earn from players without Plus. (2) Role-based cosmetics (Parent, Guard) are wearable only about 1 round in 6, which lowers their value. (3) Only R3-04 has a real social or gifting purchase loop. (4) Season passes need no countdown pressure, and past items should be buyable later. (5) The +42% adult DevEx boost will barely apply to the young-skewing themes (R3-01, R3-05). R3-03's camouflage cosmetics are the weakest structure.
